Good — atorvastatin dominates, and pitavastatin/fluvastatin have too few patients for reliable rates. Now the core query: new statin users (first-ever era per person), with a 30-day post-initiation window for (a) any statin-relevant muscle condition and (b) elevated CK measurements.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH first_stat AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, de.drug_concept_id,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY de.person_id ORDER BY de.drug_era_start_date) AS rn,
         de.drug_era_start_date AS start_dt
  FROM omop.drug_era de
  WHERE de.drug_concept_id IN (1545958,1510813,1539403,1551860,1592085)
),
newusers AS (
  SELECT person_id, drug_concept_id, start_dt FROM first_stat WHERE rn=1
),
myo AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT descendant_concept_id AS cid
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor
  WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (4347287,4345578,1077352,81286,73001)
),
cond30 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT n.person_id
  FROM newusers n
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.person_id=n.person_id
  JOIN myo ON myo.cid=co.condition_concept_id
  WHERE co.condition_start_date >= n.start_dt
    AND co.condition_start_date <= DATEADD(day,30,n.start_dt)
)
SELECT c.concept_name AS statin,
       COUNT(*) AS new_users,
       COUNT(DISTINCT cd.person_id) AS pts_with_muscle_dx_30d,
       CAST(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT cd.person_id)/COUNT(*) AS DECIMAL(6,3)) AS pct
FROM newusers n
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id=n.drug_concept_id
LEFT JOIN cond30 cd ON cd.person_id=n.person_id
GROUP BY c.concept_name
ORDER BY pct

CK is in U/L (normal upper ~200). I'll define a spike as CK >1000 U/L (marked elevation, clinically meaningful for statin myotoxicity) within 30 days of initiation. Let me run the full CK-spike analysis by statin.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH first_stat AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, de.drug_concept_id,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY de.person_id ORDER BY de.drug_era_start_date) AS rn,
         de.drug_era_start_date AS start_dt
  FROM omop.drug_era de
  WHERE de.drug_concept_id IN (1545958,1510813,1539403,1551860,1592085)
),
newusers AS (
  SELECT person_id, drug_concept_id, start_dt FROM first_stat WHERE rn=1
),
ck30 AS (
  SELECT n.person_id,
         MAX(m.value_as_number) AS max_ck
  FROM newusers n
  JOIN omop.measurement m ON m.person_id=n.person_id
  WHERE m.measurement_concept_id=3007220
    AND m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL
    AND m.unit_concept_id IN (8645,8923)
    AND m.measurement_date >= n.start_dt
    AND m.measurement_date <= DATEADD(day,30,n.start_dt)
  GROUP BY n.person_id
)
SELECT c.concept_name AS statin,
       COUNT(*) AS new_users,
       COUNT(ck.person_id) AS pts_with_ck_30d,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ck.max_ck>1000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ck_gt1000,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ck.max_ck>200 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ck_gt200,
       CAST(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN ck.max_ck>1000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(COUNT(ck.person_id),0) AS DECIMAL(6,2)) AS pct_spike_among_tested,
       CAST(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN ck.max_ck>200 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(COUNT(ck.person_id),0) AS DECIMAL(6,2)) AS pct_elevated_among_tested
FROM newusers n
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id=n.drug_concept_id
LEFT JOIN ck30 ck ON ck.person_id=n.person_id
GROUP BY c.concept_name
ORDER BY pct_spike_among_tested

I have both signals. Let me present the results.

## Statin muscle-safety signals (new-user analysis, 30-day window)

**Cohort:** first-ever statin exposure per patient (OMOP drug_era). Two independent signals within 30 days of initiation: (1) statin-relevant muscle diagnoses (myopathy/myositis/rhabdomyolysis/toxic/drug-induced), and (2) serum/plasma CK measurements.

| Statin | New users | Muscle-dx ≤30d (%) | CK-spike >1000 U/L (% of tested) | CK >200 U/L (% of tested) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Rosuvastatin** | 23,001 | 0.11% | 3.33% | 19.2% |
| **Pravastatin** | 12,596 | 0.16% | 4.51% | 20.9% |
| **Lovastatin** | 2,902 | 0.14% | 2.78%* | 27.8%* |
| **Simvastatin** | 17,234 | 0.15% | 7.71% | 25.1% |
| **Atorvastatin** | 116,171 | 0.23% | 13.04% | 36.7% |

\*Lovastatin CK rates rest on only 36 tested patients — treat as unstable.

### Answer
- **Lowest signals on both metrics: rosuvastatin and pravastatin.** Rosuvastatin has the lowest muscle-diagnosis rate (0.11%) and a low CK-spike rate (3.3%); pravastatin is close behind (0.16%; 4.5%).
- **Atorvastatin shows the highest signals** on every metric — but this is the by-far most-prescribed agent, so surveillance/testing intensity and confounding by indication inflate its apparent rates.
- **Simvastatin** sits in the middle-to-high range for CK spikes (7.7%), consistent with its known dose-dependent myotoxicity.

**Important caveats:** These are crude, unadjusted associational rates from EHR data, not causal or incidence estimates. CK "spikes" are computed only among patients who were tested (testing is itself triggered by symptoms → ascertainment bias), the 30-day window captures baseline as well as drug-related elevations, and there's no adjustment for dose, age, renal function, or interacting drugs. Pitavastatin and fluvastatin were excluded (n≈550 and 280, too small).

Want me to (a) adjust rates per patient tested vs. per new user, (b) add a formal comparison (e.g., odds ratios vs. rosuvastatin as reference), or (c) visualize this as a dashboard?
